title: Three Common Particulate Matter in Subway Environment and Their Impact on Lung Injury in Rats
content: Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a severe hazard to the human respiratory and immunological systems, and wear debris produced during the service of moving parts such as wheel-rail, brake, pantograph-catenary and so on is often regarded as the main source of subway PM. In this work, three kinds of particles (wheel-rail, brake, and pantograph-catenary friction particles) were made in laboratory to simulate the main essentials of subway particles. The physical and chemical properties of particles, including morphology, composition, and particle size, were studied Additionally, the mechanism underlying acute toxicity of particles to normal male rat lung tissue was examined. Fe and its oxides account for a large proportion of wheel-rail and braking. The particles obtained by pantograph-catenary friction are mainly Cu and its oxides, and compared with the other two kinds of particles, the proportion of small-sized particles is relatively large. The suspension of three types PM was administered through three stage inhalation rat tracheal instillation. After 24 hours, the rats were killed and detected by HE staining of lung tissue, ELISA, Tunel, and Western. In comparison to the blank control group, the rats in each group exhibited abnormal lung tissue structure following PM inhalation. This included fractured and fused alveoli, thicker alveolar walls, bleeding alveolar interstitium, and infiltration of inflammatory cells. The results showed that different PM can cause apoptosis through inflammatory reaction, and all of them can cause obvious lung damage in rats, especially pantograph-catenary PM.
